clue.text: Car fitted with storage unit for one type of sub-atomic particle

indicators.note: the car is fitted with the storage unit, so that unit goes inside the car's name

parts.note: a Lada is a Russian make of car
MB, a megabyte, is a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: A vehicle is kitted out with some storage gear to suit a physicist's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambda is a baryon, one of the many named particles studied in particle physics.

clue.text: Fruit strain found in southwest Ireland

definitions.note: a definition by location: this is a city and county in Munster

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
to rick a muscle is to strain it

explanation.surface: A variety of fruit grows in the south-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerick is an Irish city and county on the Shannon estuary in the province of Munster.

clue.text: Wearisome troubadours mostly ignored busking here?

indicators.note: mostly ignored says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tiresome wandering minstrels are largely overlooked as they play for coins underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Buskers often perform in the corridors of an underground railway such as the Paris subway.

clue.text: The most obscure band to back Springsteen went up first

indicators.note: first puts the reversed word ahead of the band
in a down clue, up says the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: slang: to pee is to go, so went can mean peed
the E Street Band backs Bruce Springsteen; E St is its short form

explanation.surface: A little-known band went up on stage before Springsteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEED to DEEP; 'went' is the slang sense of relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest can mean hardest to fathom or understand, as in deepest mystery.

clue.text: Repeatedly hit Polish journalist protecting a couple of teenagers

parts.note: to buff is to polish a surface

indicators.note: the journalist protects the teen letters by surrounding them

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

indicators.note: a couple means two, so take just the first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A shining journalist shields some young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like a nationality, but it is the verb to shine; 'a couple of' takes just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something buffeted, like a ship in a storm, is struck again and again by wind or waves.

clue.text: Peacekeepers fake cataclysmic battle making a lasting impression

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces
to forge is to fake

indicators.note: cataclysmic says the letters of the battle are thrown into upheaval

explanation.surface: United Nations troops stage a sham disastrous war that stays in the memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cataclysmic' rearranges BATTLE to TTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unforgettable stays in the mind for ever, leaving a mark that endures.

clue.text: Massively reducing consumption quickly weighs down elected government

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the rest, pressing down on them

parts.note: fast means quickly
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A hasty crash diet is pressing on a newly chosen administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food sharply cuts what one eats, the strictest kind of diet.

clue.text: Leaves Texan city before last third of song

parts.note: tea is made from dried leaves

indicators.note: take only the part of the city's name that comes before its final third

parts.note: Fort Worth is a city in Texas

explanation.surface: Someone departs a Texas city just before the last part of a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: FORTWORTH has nine letters; dropping its last third, RTH, leaves FORTWO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous 1925 Youmans and Caesar number from the musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Occasionally sees a spy following academic in fancy clothing

indicators.note: the picked letters follow the academic's title

parts.note: DR, doctor, is an academic title

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Now and then a spy is seen tailing a professor in a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy describes smart, elaborate clothing worn for a formal occasion.

clue.text: To smart set, feta crumbling is what's of great importance

indicators.note: feta crumbles easily, and crumbling here says all these letters break up and re-form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashionable people think the way their feta crumbles is a vital matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters run across 'To smart set, feta', fourteen in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs of government are proverbially the weightiest concerns, so the phrase covers anything of serious consequence.

clue.text: American military leaders visit Russia, worried over promises of weapons for Japan

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part above the second
the leaders go into the jumbled country, as visitors do
worried says the letters of Russia are fretted into a new order
leaders picks the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: words, as in giving one's word, are promises

explanation.surface: US generals call on Moscow, fretting about pledges of arms to Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives SURAIS, which the American military leaders' initials then visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved katana was the blade carried by Japan's feudal warrior class.

clue.text: See 9
Finally discover hotel with BBC channel's French stream

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word discover

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
BBC One is the main British public television channel

explanation.surface: A traveller ends up finding a hotel that gets a BBC channel by a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river flowing through south-east France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: I'm surprised by king having cricketers as fanatically loyal warriors

parts.note: the exclamation 'my!' expresses surprise
R, from Latin rex, is king
mid-ons are fielders placed on the leg side near the bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a monarch who keeps cricketers as devoted fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position, and its plural MID-ONS stands for the players placed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Myrmidons were Achilles's devoted soldiers, and the name now means blindly faithful followers.

clue.text: Bar with returning soldier in the balance

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a pub or shop

indicators.note: returning says the soldier-in-the group is read from back to front
the soldier sits in the word the

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A bar with a soldier coming back hangs in the balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the balance' reads as one idiom, but it splits into an indicator, the word to be reversed, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterweight is a mass that offsets another, so it acts as a balance.

clue.text: Having a chill victory in finance having the cap removed

indicators.note: the victory goes in the trimmed finance word
the cap is the top letter, so the first letter is taken off

parts.note: funding is finance
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Someone wins a cold while their budget is stripped of its ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having the cap removed' takes F off FUNDING to give UNDING; 'chill' is the slang sense of relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill out is slang for relaxing, and relaxing after work is the same as winding down.

clue.text: Perhaps compound revolutionary's revolutionary claim

definitions.note: a compound is one example of a substance of this kind, hence perhaps

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary here says the letters of claim are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel's radical assertion is perhaps a mix of ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: first Che, then the signal that rearranges CLAIM into MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound is one example of a substance produced by reactions in a laboratory.

clue.text: Bear with 9 being difficult as optimism returns about Obama's leadership

indicators.note: the number sits inside the word with, being contained by it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: difficult says the letters of the number are made awkward and jumbled

parts.note: the number 9 spelled out as a word

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about the leading letter
returns says the word for optimism is read backwards

parts.note: hope is optimism

indicators.note: leadership picks the first letter of Obama's

explanation.surface: A grizzly with a number causes trouble as hope fades around Obama's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is the number itself, not a reference to 9 across; 'returns' gives EPOH, which goes about Obama's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A.A. Milne's honey-loving teddy is perhaps the best-known bear in children's literature.

clue.text: New York (Queens) embassy opening for former African leader

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen, so two queens give the pair

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of embassy

explanation.surface: An embassy opens in the New York borough of Queens for a past African head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens looks like the New York borough, but as a plural it is ER twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Nyerere led Tanzania from independence until 1985.

clue.text: Politicians' composure disturbed following company's withdrawal

definitions.note: the clue's plural possessive stands for the plural noun for these members of parliament

indicators.note: disturbed says the remaining letters of composure are unsettled into a new order
withdrawal says the company letters are taken out of composure

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Politicians lose their calm after a firm pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal' takes CO out of COMPOSURE, and 'disturbed' rearranges the MPOSURE left.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the European Parliament are elected representatives, a kind of legislator.

clue.text: Have the means to remove thoroughfare from Midlands town

indicators.note: remove says the street letters are taken off the town

parts.note: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands
ST, street, is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A town council can pay to close a road in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire, in England's Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to pay for something is to have the money or means for it.

clue.text: Spider play has been rejected, blocked by heartless law

parts.note: play and fun are both amusement

indicators.note: the reversed word is blocked by the law letters placed in its middle
rejected says the word been is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A play about a spider has been turned down because a gutted law got in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link; 'rejected' gives NEEB, and 'heartless' leaves only the outside letters of law.
explanation.definitionFit: The funnel-web is a highly venomous Australian arachnid that spins a tube-shaped web.

clue.text: Back manager initially to make changes at Arsenal

parts.note: rear and back both mean the hind part

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of manager

explanation.surface: A football coach is backed at first to reshape Arsenal's squad.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, but here an arsenal is a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Restocking a weapons store is equipping again with weaponry, a playful view of changes to an arsenal.

clue.text: Army not gracious after acting officer makes sacrifices here?

indicators.note: the shortened army comes after the officer

parts.note: LT, lieutenant, is an officer

indicators.note: not says the gracious word is left out of army

parts.note: 'my!' and 'gracious!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A rude army follows a temporary commander who sacrifices men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes MY from ARMY to leave AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the raised table where offerings and sacrifices are made in worship.

clue.text: Essentially hoping experts will deliver a verdict

indicators.note: essentially points to the core letters of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Fundamentally, people hope specialists will give their judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the heart of each word: OPIN, hoping without its ends, and E, the central letter of experts.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, much as a judge or expert gives a ruling.

clue.text: Arthritic mice hurt badly after swallowing dose of analgesic

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the first letter once they have swallowed it
badly says the letters of mice hurt are put in a poor order
a dose is a small amount, here just the first letter of the painkiller

explanation.surface: Sore mice are in a bad way after taking a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges MICE HURT, and 'after swallowing' puts A, the first letter of 'analgesic', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes joint pain and stiffness, the very complaint suffered by arthritis sufferers.

clue.text: Get rid of lubrication when in the last stages of qualification

indicators.note: the short word is inserted near the end of the qualification

parts.note: a degree is a university qualification
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A student clears away grease while finishing a course.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrease is to clean oil and grease from something, removing its lubricant.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon pilot missing one of the stars

indicators.note: missing says a letter is taken out of the pilot word

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a trial
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Old English aviator flies off without one star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes I out of TRIAL to give TRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is an adjective describing celestial bodies, from Latin astrum, star.
